event_date_text: About UNRWA Toggle submenu Mandate and History Toggle submenu Mandate History Mandate and History UNRWA is the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East. The United Nations General Assembly established UNRWA in 1949 with a mandate to provide humanitarian assistance and protection to registered Palestine Refugees in the Agency’s area of operations pending a just and lasting solution to their plight. Principles and Values Toggle submenu Humanitarian Principles Sustainable Development Goals Principles and Values As an Agency with a humanitarian mandate – to assist and protect Palestine Refugees – humanitarian principles provide the space to make our work possible. From ensuring the sanctity of our shelters in times of crisis, to maintaining access to the most vulnerable populations, to advocating on behalf of Palestine Refugees, the principles of humanity , impartiality , neutrality , and independence are at the heart of all UNRWA operations. Leadership Toggle submenu Our leadership Organisational structure Leadership UNRWA is led by a Commissioner-General, appointed by the UN Secretary-General. The Commissioner-General is supported by a Deputy Commissioner-General for Programmes and Partnerships and a Deputy Commissioner-General for Operational Support. Funding Toggle submenu How we are funded How we spend funds Our partners Funding UNRWA is funded almost entirely by voluntary contributions, mostly from government donors. Accountability Toggle submenu Colonna Report Advisory Commission Internal oversight Ethics office Dispute Tribunal Work with us Toggle submenu Careers Procurement Key areas of work What we do UNRWA’s key services include education, healthcare, relief and social services, infrastructure and camp improvement, microfinance, and emergency response. It also elects the Members of the Executive Board and appoints, every four years, the Director-General. The working languages of the General Conference are Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish. The General Conference consists of the representatives of UNESCO's Member States. It meets every two years, and is attended by Member States and Associate Members, together with observers for non-Member States, intergovernmental organizations and non-governmental organizations (NGOs). Each country has one vote, irrespective of its size or the extent of its contribution to the budget. On 30 September 2026, distinguished economist Edward Miguel delivers WIDER Annual Lecture 30, Can Africa escape the climate–conflict–poverty trap? In this lecture, Edward Miguel examines how rising temperatures, economic stress, and armed conflict interact to produce a vicious cycle that threatens long-term development, with a particular focus on Africa.
